name: Greater Boise Auditorium District
tax_rate: 5% auditorium district tax on short-term lodging (30 days or less) within district boundaries (Boise and Garden City), including nonsleeping/meeting rooms; collected by the Idaho State Tax Commission (Form 1250). Lodging guests also pay the 2% state Travel and Convention tax and 6% state sales tax.
deadline_pattern: No application cycle. The board allocates hotel tax revenue through its annual budget (fiscal year ends November 30; budget presentation each November) to Boise Centre operations, debt, capital and a contract with Visit Boise.
annual_pool: No grant pool. FY2025 district lodging tax revenue was $12,098,961; FY2026 forecast $12.4M. Outside spending is limited to the Visit Boise CVB contract ($1,104,000 base in FY2026, up to $1,129,000 with bonuses) and a short list of event sponsorships (Big Sky Conference basketball tournament, Treefort Music Fest, Boise Metro Chamber, Idaho Business Review, Peak 43) with amounts not published.
contact: Cody Lund, Executive Director, Boise Centre and Greater Boise Auditorium District, clund@boisecentre.com, (208) 336-8900 (district office, 850 W Front St, Boise)
notes: GBAD owns and runs Boise Centre and uses its 5% hotel tax for the convention center, its financed purchase debt (balance $14.5M), capital ($3.9M budgeted for 2026, including the Idaho Central Aquatics Center) and a roughly $1.1M annual Visit Boise contract. It holds large reserves ($16.3M committed, $21.0M unassigned at Nov 30, 2025) and has spent nearly two years deciding how to use them, while opposing a 2026 Boise State attempt to tap the tax. There is no event or sponsorship application; the few sponsorships it carries (Big Sky tournament, Treefort) are board-negotiated. An outside event's realistic route is Visit Boise's sports event sponsorship form or the ITC grant through a nonprofit DMO.

meeting_schedule: Regular board meeting monthly, generally a Thursday afternoon at Boise Centre (next listed: Thursday Nov 19, 2026, 2:00 pm MST); agendas, minutes and recordings at boiseauditorium.com/meetings/
pool_note: FY2025 (year ended Nov 30, 2025) district lodging tax was $12,098,961. All of it is committed to Boise Centre operations, debt service ($1,218,950 principal plus $398,945 interest in FY2025), capital and the Visit Boise contract ($1,050,411 paid in FY2025). No dollars are open to outside applicants, so the competitive pool is zero.

name: Pocatello-Chubbuck Auditorium District
tax_rate: 5% auditorium district tax on short-term lodging at hotels and motels within district boundaries (Pocatello and Chubbuck); collected by the Idaho State Tax Commission (Form 4250). Guests also pay the 2% state Travel and Convention tax and 6% state sales tax.
deadline_pattern: No application cycle. Room tax proceeds operate and market the district-owned Mountain View Event Center; the board invites groups wanting to host regional or national events to contact the center, which is a venue booking conversation rather than a grant.
annual_pool: No grant pool. Tax Commission distributions were about $1.59M gross in FY2026 ($1.61M in FY2025); all of it goes to Mountain View Event Center operations and marketing.
contact: Shelton Robinson, Executive Director, Mountain View Event Center / PCAD; Alisa Hardy, Business Manager and Secretary/Treasurer; office 208-235-7659, 1567 Way to Grace Ave, Pocatello, ID 83201 (no staff emails published; contact form on site)
notes: Voters created the district in 1998. The 5% room tax built and now runs the Mountain View Event Center (28,000 sq ft hardwood gym, 26,000 sq ft turf fieldhouse, about 1,000 bleacher seats) and funds its marketing; no sponsorship or grant program for outside events exists on the district site, in its 2026 agendas, or in local coverage. The five-member elected board meets the third Friday of the month (third Thursday June-September) at 9:00 am. Events wanting lodging-tax-backed support in Pocatello should go through the Greater Pocatello CVB (Visit Pocatello), which received $265,517 in 2026 ITC grant money.
meeting_schedule: Regular board meeting third Friday of each month at 9:00 am MST (third Thursday June through September) at Mountain View Event Center, 1567 Way to Grace Ave, Pocatello; 2026 agendas posted at pocatellochubbuckad.com/board-of-directors/meetings/ (no minutes posted)
pool_note: About $1.59M gross FY2026 hotel tax per Idaho State Tax Commission distributions (per the project's source list), all applied to event center operations and marketing. Nothing is open to outside applicants.

name: McCall
tax_rate: Lodging in McCall pays 7% city LOT: 3% Tourism (Lodging) LOT (Jan 1, 2019 to Dec 31, 2028, held in trust for the grant program) plus the Streets LOT share on lodging (3% through Dec 31, 2026, rising to 4% under Ordinance 1028 approved May 20, 2025 for Jan 1, 2026 to Dec 31, 2036; city pages are inconsistent on 7% vs 8%) and the 1% general retail LOT. From June 1, 2026 the Mountain Community Center District adds a 5% auditorium district tax. Plus 2% state Travel and Convention tax and 6% state sales tax.
deadline_pattern: Applications for the following fiscal year (Oct 1 to Sep 30) open in February (city page says February 11; older page said March 1) and are due April 30; the LOT Commission hears applicant presentations by May 31 and sends recommendations to City Council by June 30, which adopts them at its late-June budget meeting and approves funding contracts in July
typical_open: Mid-February (FY2027 application period is now closed; FY2028 round expected to open February 2027)
annual_pool: FY2027: $1,000,000 total Tourism LOT appropriation, of which $332,500 followed LOT Commission recommendations ($302,872 to 20 outside applications plus $29,628 to the city housing fund) and $667,500 went to staff-recommended city items. FY2026: about $900,000 revenue (later amended to $1.2M), with $315,000 split by the Commission among 32 applications and $585,000 reserved for city departments.
contact: Cari Tassano, LOT/STR Administrator, City Clerk's Office, 208-634-8520 (email via city site); City of McCall Clerk's Office, 216 E Park St, McCall, ID 83638, 208-634-7142
notes: McCall runs Idaho's most developed resort-city grant program: the 3% Tourism LOT is held in trust and a seven-member citizen LOT Commission scores written requests against eight public purposes (streets, cultural and recreational facilities, recreation and cultural services, parks, animal shelter, housing, marketing and event promotion, tourism impacts). Council has steadily shifted the pool toward city uses, taking about 60 percent in FY2026 and two-thirds in FY2027 for transit, sidewalks, housing and STR compliance software, so the competitive share is roughly $300,000 a year across 20 to 32 applications. Awards skew to recreation nonprofits (Manchester Ice and Event Centre, ski club, youth hockey), events (Winter Carnival logistics, Summer Music Festival, Kaleidascope) and public safety (search and rescue, avalanche center); typical grants run $1,000 to $30,000. The chamber's Winter Carnival request was cut from $35,000 to $14,000 in FY2026 and funded at $20,000 for restrooms and traffic control in FY2027.
members_source: Commission chair from Valley Lookout, Sept 9, 2025 (https://valleylookout.com/2025/09/09/sharlies-fan-club-winter-carnival-seeking-donations-to-save-parade/); 2025 appointments from McCall Agenda Bill Report AB 25-042 (https://www.mccall.id.us/DocumentCenter/View/2628/Agenda-Bill-Report-20251007); council from Valley Lookout Jan 14, 2026 (https://valleylookout.com/?p=8134). Full seven-member roster is in the city's LOT Commissioners PDF (https://www.mccall.id.us/DocumentCenter/View/2568/LOT-Commissioners), which could not be read.

presentation.pattern: City Code 4.12.6 requires at least one public LOT Commission meeting by May 31 to hear applicant presentations and review requests (2026 Commission meetings were posted for March 4, May 27 and June 3); recommendations are presented to Council at the late-June budget meeting (June 25, 2026 for FY2027)
presentation.format: In-person presentation to the LOT Commission at McCall City Hall; length not published

meeting_schedule: LOT Commission meets as needed around the annual cycle: by March 15 to review the Clerk's revenue estimate, by April 30 to set the request deadline, by May 31 for applicant presentations, by June 30 to send recommendations (2026 agendas posted for Mar 4, May 27 and Jun 3); City Council meets second and fourth Thursdays
pool_note: FY2027 (Oct 2026 to Sep 2027) Tourism LOT expenditures budgeted at $1,000,000 in the July 23, 2026 council packet (AB 26-253). Staff items took $667,500 (Treasure Valley Transit operations $188,000 and marketing $4,000, Streets LOT support $14,500, STR tracking software $20,500, downtown sidewalk maintenance $285,000, city housing program $155,500). The LOT Commission recommended $332,500, of which $29,628 went to the City of McCall housing fund, leaving $302,872 across 20 outside applications (including $79,600 as a Treasure Valley Transit grant match and $20,000 to the McCall Area Chamber). FY2026 collections were budgeted at $1.0M and amended to $1.2M in August 2026.

name: Nampa Auditorium District
tax_rate: 5% hotel room tax on short-term lodging within district boundaries (drawn around the Ford Idaho Center and Nampa Civic Center); Idaho State Tax Commission administers from the April 2026 return (Form 4350). Guests also pay the 2% state Travel and Convention tax and 6% state sales tax.
deadline_pattern: The district posts formal Requests for Funding twice a year (spring solicitation due April 1, 2026; fall solicitation due October 30, 2026 at 5:00 pm MT), but they are capital funding requests from the public entities that own or operate the two district venues (City of Nampa for the Civic Center, College of Western Idaho for the Ford Idaho Center), not grants to outside event organizers
typical_open: Spring round posted around February (Funding Process document on the Feb 9, 2026 agenda); fall round posted in early autumn
annual_pool: Backers projected about $1.2M to $1.5M per year; about $700K collected in the first year. Fall 2026 requests on file: CWI asked $700,000 per year for ten years ($7M) for Ford Idaho Center capital projects; City of Nampa applied for Nampa Civic Center auditorium improvements. No award amounts published yet.
contact: Nampa Auditorium District administrative team, info@nampaauditoriumdistrict.gov; board seat emails seat1@ through seat5@nampaauditoriumdistrict.gov; no phone published
notes: Voters created the district Nov 5, 2024 (about 62% yes) and the five-member elected board first met Jan 13, 2025. Statute limits spending to auditorium and community center facilities, so its Request for Funding rounds are effectively a capital program for the Ford Idaho Center (now transferred from the City of Nampa to College of Western Idaho) and the Nampa Civic Center. The Oct 30, 2026 round drew a $7M ten-year ask from CWI for a pavilion, RV and horse stall expansions, kitchen and amphitheater, and a City of Nampa Civic Center auditorium application. Event producers cannot apply; the Nampa Chamber (2026 ITC grantee, $143,450) is the lodging-tax-funded marketing partner.

name: Victor
tax_rate: 8% on lodging and short-term rentals (30 days or less) from 2026, up from 6% (Ordinance O642, approved Nov 4, 2025, sunset extended to July 1, 2050); 1% on liquor by the drink and other retail sales (2018 Resort Tax). Plus 2% state Travel and Convention tax and 6% state sales tax.
deadline_pattern: Community Grant applications are due on or before June 1 each year (FY2024 deadline was June 8, 2023); a City Council subcommittee scores them, awards are finalized when Council adopts the budget in August, and funds are disbursed through the Community Foundation of Teton Valley's Tin Cup Challenge the following summer unless the recipient asks otherwise
typical_open: Spring (call for applications posted in May)
annual_pool: Community Fund set at roughly 3.5% of the annual LOT budget; grants generally $7,500 or less per organization. With LOT running about $700,000 a year the fund is on the order of $25,000. No award list published.
contact: Submit to Michelle Smith, City Clerk, michelles@victoridaho.gov, 208-274-7082 ext. 4; questions to Jeremy Besbris, City Administrator, jeremyb@victoridaho.gov, ext. 7, or Jasmine Griffin, City Treasurer, treasurer@victoridaho.gov, ext. 5; Victor City Hall, 138 N Main St, PO Box 122, Victor, ID 83455
notes: Victor's LOT (about $3.47M spent since 2020, roughly $700K a year, dominated by the lodging tier) mostly funds streets, equipment, facilities, housing and contracted law enforcement, with 'visitor services and promotion' a permitted use. The only application-based piece is the Community Grants program, a small nonprofit fund (about 3.5% of the LOT budget, grants up to about $7,500) scored on a 100-point rubric by a Council subcommittee and paid out through the Tin Cup Challenge. For-profits, individuals, political groups and private schools are excluded. Mayor Will Frohlich resigned in June 2026 and Council appointed Sue Muncaster mayor on July 8, 2026, so the roster is in flux.

presentation.pattern: Written application scored by a Council subcommittee; no presentation requirement stated
presentation.format: Written application on the city form (Municode library)

meeting_schedule: City Council meets the second and fourth Wednesday of each month at 6:00 pm at City Hall, 138 N Main St; agendas posted the Friday before
pool_note: LOT revenue is about $700,000 a year (city reports $3.47M spent across categories since 2020). The Community Fund is set at about 3.5% of the annual LOT budget, which works out to roughly $24,500; the exact FY2026 or FY2027 figure is in the budget book (Municode) and was not read. Grants are capped at about $7,500 per organization.

notes: Bellevue's small lodging LOT (about $65,000 to $83,000 a year) is locked to streets and snow removal and has never funded events. The 2025 expansion failed by 15 votes and in August 2026 the council began discussing a repeat measure (lodging to 6%, five-year term, no food and drink taxes) for a May ballot with a March 13 filing deadline, though staff earlier said a new measure could not go to voters before November 2027. name: Mountain Community Center District
tax_rate: 5% auditorium district tax on short-term lodging in the McCall-Donnelly area of north Valley County (district spans Valley and Adams counties, including Tamarack and Brundage), effective June 1, 2026, collected by the Idaho State Tax Commission (Form 4450). Stacks on McCall's 7% city LOT (13% local in McCall, 9% in Donnelly) plus the 2% state Travel and Convention tax and 6% sales tax.
deadline_pattern: No grant program; the district is saving its lodging tax toward a 120,000 sq ft indoor fieldhouse and convention facility estimated at $20M to $35M, with construction three to five years out
annual_pool: Projected about $1.5M per year once collections mature; first month (June 2026) was $52,105 per the Tax Commission. No grants.
contact: Megan Lawler, board secretary (staff); no phone or email published; letter-of-intent and land-offer forms at mountaincommunitycenter.com
notes: Voters approved the district Nov 4, 2025 (1,760 to 1,008, about 64%) and the five elected directors were sworn in Feb 24, 2026. It cannot levy property tax, so the 5% lodging tax is its only revenue; the board solicited land offers of 10 acres or more (due April 16, 2026) with candidate sites on Lake Fork Road, in McCall city limits and near the Activity Barn on Brundage land. Phase one is an open fieldhouse that can host trade shows and community events, so it is a future venue partner for McCall-area events, not a funder.
meeting_schedule: Board meetings began Feb 24, 2026; schedule not published online as of this check
pool_note: About $1.5M a year projected at full collection (June 2026 first-month receipts $52,105). Every dollar is reserved for the fieldhouse project; nothing for outside applicants.

name: Stanley
tax_rate: 2.5% city option tax on all sales subject to Idaho sales tax, including lodging, retail and event tickets (city example: $5.00 on a $200 stay; $500 on $20,000 in event tickets); renewed by voters Nov 3, 2020 for ten years (through 2031). Plus 2% state Travel and Convention tax and 6% state sales tax.
deadline_pattern: City-based organizations file an Option Tax Financial Support Request Form with the City Clerk; requests are considered during budget development (spring to summer) and the subsequent funds distribution process, with the budget adopted at a mid-August public hearing (Aug 14, 2025 for FY26; Aug 13, 2026 for FY27)
typical_open: Spring, ahead of the city budget process (form available from the city office year-round)
annual_pool: Option tax is almost half of all city revenue ($300,156 spent FY2018-19; $350,000 budgeted FY2019-20; peak months $65K-$115K in summer 2024). FY2027 appropriation ordinance shows an Option Tax line of about $138,000. No award list published.
contact: Hannah Menzel, City Clerk, cityclerk@cityofstanleyid.gov, 208-774-2286; Savannah Pedersen, Treasurer; PO Box 53, 510 Eva Falls Ave, Stanley, ID 83278 (summer hours Mon-Thu 8-4, winter 9-3)
notes: Stanley's 2.5% option tax is capped by the ballot language to the city park, cemetery, streets, snow grooming, law enforcement, grant matches, community building and recreation facilities (Pioneer Park, Valley Creek Preserve, Central Idaho Dark Sky Reserve), workforce housing infrastructure, recycling, and 'city-based organizations.' That last clause is the grant route: the chamber, library, fire and EMS volunteers request support on a city form and the Council sizes awards during the budget. It is informal, with no deadline, rubric or published award list, and funds can be used as matches for other grants. Events should expect to route a request through the Stanley-Sawtooth Chamber (a $180,000 ITC grantee in 2026) rather than apply directly.
